pr_title: fix pv-binder-controller delete new created PV when controller is on heavy loader
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

fix pv-binder-controller delete new created PV when controller is on heavy loader

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #83177

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

1. The [cache](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L181) in the controller should be update immediately when received event from informer. Update the cache item when controller/worker processing the item may cause a long latency to update the item in the cache, because the controller/worker may on heavy load state and busy with processing backlog items.
2. The new created PV has no annotation `pv.kubernetes.io/bound-by-controller`

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
fix pv-binder-controller delete new created PV when controller is on heavy loader
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

None

issue_context.title: CRITICAL!! PV-Binder-Controller will delete the new created PV
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

[PV-Binder-Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go) will delete the new created (unused and unbound) PV if PV-Binder-Controller is on heavy load, when the PV related StorageClass ReclaimPolicy is OnDelete.



**What you expected to happen**:

Fix this critical bug to avoid to delete PV in mistake.



**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

We need to make [PV-Binder-Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go) on heavy load to reproduce this issue, actually 100 PVC/PV creation in same time will make [PV-Binder-Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go) to be this heavy load state.  I will share the PV-Loader project to [perf-tests](https://github.com/kubernetes/perf-tests) later.



- Background

[PV-Binder-Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go) actual has two Queue which are PV and PVC Queue, and combine two controllers to [PV-Binder-Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go). I called these two controllers to `PV-Controller` and `PVC-Controller` respectively. `PVC-Controller` has some performance issue, it process PVC may cost a long latency(I will post another issue to talk about the performance of [PV-Binder-Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go)). However, `PV-Controller` performance is better than `PVC-Controller`, it process PV is faster than `PVC-Controller`.

These two controller get PVC from the inner [cache](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L181) firstly, and only in same cases will get PVC from Informer Lister and API Server. And a PVC in [cache](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L181)  will only be updated when `PVC-Controller` finished processed this PVC.



- Bug timeline

1. User create a PVC (StorageClass RelaimPolicy is OnDelete)
2. CSI Provisioner create a pre-bound PV
3. `PVC-Controller` is busy with processing another backlog PVCs, and the created PVC is not updated in [cache](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L181) .
4. `PV-Controller` process the created PV,  can't get the related PVC, treat the PV as Released and reclaimVolume, then if the StorageClass RelaimPolicy is OnDelete, delete the PV. Code at [PVC-Binder-Controller#L522 - L583](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L522)



- Examples

1. StorageClass

```yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: foo
provisioner: foo-csi
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
```

2. PVC

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: test-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 3Mi
  storageClassName: foo
```

2. PV provisioned by CSI Provisioner according PVC

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-for-test-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  capacity:
    storage: 3Mi
  claimRef:
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    name: test-pvc
    namespace: default
    resourceVersion: "1"
    uid: "foo-uid"
  csi:
    ...
```





**Anything else we need to know?**:

1. I will post another issue to talk about the performance of [PV-Binder-Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go).
2. I will post PV-Loader performance tests to [perf-tests](https://github.com/kubernetes/perf-tests).



**Environment**:

No need to care about this.
comments:
> Bug timeline
> 1. User create a PVC (StorageClass RelaimPolicy is OnDelete)
> 2. CSI Provisioner create a pre-bound PV
> 3. PVC-Controller is busy with processing another backlog PVCs
> 4. PV-Controller process the created PV, can't get the related PVC, treat the PV as Released and reclaimVolume

Something does not sound right between steps 1. and 2. The external provisioning is initiated by the PVC controller itself. It gets a PVC, checks it does not know how to provision it and adds an annotation that it should be provisioned externally. So the PVC controller has seen the PVC and should have it in its cache.

In theory this should be pretty robust. There must be a bug somewhere. Did the controller forgot to add the PVC to the controller cache? Was the PVC deleted from the cache? Or does the external provisioner start provisioning without the [external provisioning annotation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad333ac4217f442b56a5dac8407617ba359e6e17/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/util/util.go#L70)?
What version of CSI provisioner are you using? There was a bug in older releases in the lib-external-provisioner where it was not checking for the annotation.
What version of Kubernetes are you using?

@answer1991 can you please specify the CSI driver you are using and it's version?
Do you happen to be using something like EBS CSI or GCE PD CSI by any chance?

PV controller should have seen the pvc. But this is a pre-bind pv, so may be not. 


See the codes and the comments.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L524-532

From the comments, we should `double check` pvc when pvc it not found and the pv is bound by` external binder`.

But from the codes, we should `double check` pvc when pvc is not found and pv is bound by `controller`?

> Or does the external provisioner start provisioning without the [external provisioning annotation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad333ac4217f442b56a5dac8407617ba359e6e17/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/util/util.go#L70)?

> There was a bug in older releases in the lib-external-provisioner where it was not checking for the annotation.

Yes, I checked and found our external provisioner start to provision without this annotation. Our CSI components' lib version is 0.4.0, it is alpha version?

I should fix our external provisioner to provision PVs only when PVCs has annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner`

@msau42 @jsafrane @alejandrox1

The fix to check for the annotation was made here: https://github.com/kubernetes-incubator/external-storage/pull/521 which was release with external-storage v5.5.0.  CSI external-provisioner v0.4.x [imports v5.2.0](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-provisioner/blob/release-0.4/Gopkg.toml#L41) which does not contain the fix.  CSI external-provisioner v1.0+ should have the fix.

review_comments:
The original codes seem not consistent with the following comments.

Is `!found && !metav1.HasAnnotation(volume.ObjectMeta, pvutil.AnnBoundByController)` right ?

hi, you should add `pvutil.AnnBoundByController` annotation in your external PV binder. With this annotation, PV controller will go into this block and check apiserver if not found in informer cache. This is required to work well with Kubernetes PV controller: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/32ffe47fd2d124096f42d843f29d6b123b901d52/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/util/util.go#L48-L50.

This annotation is used to distinguish from PVs & PVCs bound manually, e.g. create PVC with PV bound.

Actually, I does not use any external PV binder, I use CSI provisioner to create PV then meet this bug. PVs that provisioned by CSI provisioner does not have this annotation:

https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-provisioner/blob/e17cc20ee72c6c0bb27a3cf81348f40834925136/vendor/sigs.k8s.io/sig-storage-lib-external-provisioner/controller/controller.go#L1280-L1281

And for now, there is no way to develop our  external PV binder, because the pv-binder-controller will take over all PVC/PVs and there is no way to skip pv-binder-controller management to use our external PV binder.

oh, I see the problem. External provisioner created volumes with `ClaimRef` filled and wait for the PV controller to bind them with PVCs. However, PV controller will reclaim these PVs if they don't see the related PVCs in `ctrl.claims`. (PV is created by external provisioner after dynamic provisioning is triggered and before PVC is put into `ctrl.claims`?)

If this can happen, I think to remove `metav1.HasAnnotation(volume.ObjectMeta, pvutil.AnnBoundByController)` is enough here because it will check informer cache, no need to update `ctrl.claims` in informer listeners (informer cache is updated first).

Alternatively, we can ignore PVs not bound by PV controller and don't reclaim them [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/654aa1d846a72ba842967424d287304db1dad803/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L565-L588).

cc @msau42 @jsafrane What's your opinions?

> PV is created by external provisioner after dynamic provisioning is triggered and before PVC is put into ctrl.claims?

Yes, this is the bug root case.

> no need to update ctrl.claims in informer listeners

I think the reason why the controller need `ctrl.claims` is that the controller want to get the latest version of PVC/PV, update the cache when controller finish updating PVC/PV is only guaranteed when update by pv-bind-controller side. But on the other side, any other controller may also update PVC/PVs and pv-bind-controller receive the update event, in that case we need update `ctrl.claims` also.

> we can ignore PVs not bound by PV controller and don't reclaim them

Actually, I'm draft a KEP to make possible to develop a high performance component to  manage PVC/PV lifecycle, typically for CSI volumes. And for now, there is no way to develop our external PV binder, and the pv-bind-controller performance does not meet our requirement, performance issue see #83178.
